name: Information availability

subjectOf.text: Dynamic elements in the rulemaking process increase the availability of relevant information for rulemaking and thereby improve institutional design.
subjectOf.abstract: Dynamic elements in the rulemaking process may increase the availability of relevant information for rulemaking and may improve institutional design.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Law Dynamic Regulation in a New Institutional Economics Framework (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2267560

subjectOf.text: Feedback effects in decentralized systems raise the availability of relevant information for governance rules ex ante and allow necessary revisions to be anticipated before rules emerge as suboptimal, rather than acquiring that information ex post.
subjectOf.abstract: Rather than acquiring the necessary information ex-post after rules have emerged as suboptimal, feedback effects help increase the availability of relevant information for governance rules ex-ante and anticipate necessary revisions before rules emerge as suboptimal.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain-Based Corporate Governance (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3441904
scope_conditions: dynamic decentralized governance frameworks with peer to peer information transfer
